title: 4GE1-style exam questions: economic sectors, change and population theories (Paper 2, Topics 4.1 and 4.2)
subject: Geography
source: Seeded from geography/y11 lesson 29 (Own 4GE1-style exam questions with indicative mark points (portal printable))
intro: Lesson 29: Revision: economic sectors, change and population theories (Paper 2, Topics 4.1 and 4.2). Answer every question. Show your working. Mark it with the mark scheme and log any errors in your repair list.

questions.q: 'Assess the reasons for changes in employment structure in one named country.' Portal response box.
questions.a: Named country; reasons such as globalisation, mechanisation, resource depletion, policy, rising incomes; evidence; judgement on the most important reason
questions.model: Teacher plans: intro (named country and its change); P1 globalisation; P2 mechanisation and resources; P3 policy and incomes; conclusion: most important reason with justification.

questions.q: Compare the views of Malthus and Boserup.
questions.a: Malthus: population outstrips food, leading to checks; Boserup: pressure brings innovation; evidence for each; comparison words

questions.q: Explain why informal employment is common in megacities in developing countries.
questions.a: Rapid migration brings more workers than formal jobs (1); low skills and few contracts (1); informal work is the only option to earn (1)

questions.q: Explain one cause of the growth of the tertiary sector in developed countries.
questions.a: Rising incomes increase demand for services such as leisure and health (1), so more jobs are created in services (1)
questions.model: Cause: people earn more. Effect: they spend more on services. Result: tertiary jobs grow.

questions.q: Give one characteristic of informal employment.
questions.a: For example: no contract, no tax paid, irregular income

questions.q: State one piece of evidence that supports Boserup.
questions.a: The Green Revolution (1): new seeds, fertiliser and irrigation raised yields as population grew (1)

questions.q: Big question: will the world run out of food, or will people always find a way?
questions.a: A reasoned view using Malthus and Boserup, with evidence such as the Green Revolution and ongoing food insecurity
